evals.prompt: We are building a React SPA that calls our own backend REST/HTTP API on API Gateway (the browser does NOT call S3 or DynamoDB directly). An engineer created BOTH a Cognito User Pool (with an app client secret + `response_type=token` implicit grant storing tokens in `localStorage`) AND a Cognito Identity Pool with unauthenticated guest access enabled! Audit every mistake and give the clean Cognito architecture.
expectations: Activates the aws-auth skill

Explains **User Pool vs Identity Pool**: since the React SPA only calls your own API, **only a Cognito User Pool is needed** (an Identity Pool is only for vending temporary STS AWS credentials when clients call S3/DynamoDB directly; disable/remove the unnecessary Identity Pool and unauthenticated guest role)

Fixes all 3 SPA OAuth/session anti-patterns: use a **public app client with NO client secret**, replace deprecated `response_type=token` implicit grant with **Authorization Code Grant + PKCE (`response_type=code`)**, and replace `localStorage` with `cookieStorage` + **refresh token rotation** + **token revocation**

evals.prompt: A teammate ran `aws cognito-idp update-user-pool-client --user-pool-id ap-south-1_abc123 --client-id 4xyz --callback-urls https://app.example.com/callback` just to update 1 callback URL, and suddenly production token refresh, `ExplicitAuthFlows`, and custom token lifetimes all broke! Explain why and show the mandatory safe update pattern.
expectations: Activates the aws-auth skill

Explains the critical full-replace behavior: **`update-user-pool-client` (and `set-identity-pool-roles`) are FULL REPLACE operations, NOT partial patches** — any omitted field silently resets to service defaults (`ExplicitAuthFlows`, token validity, `EnableTokenRevocation`, refresh token rotation, read/write attributes)!

Demonstrates the mandatory **read-modify-write** workflow: call `describe-user-pool-client` (or `get-identity-pool-roles`) first, merge your change into the complete existing configuration object, and pass every field back

evals.prompt: Users sign in cleanly via our Cognito User Pool (`ap-south-1_Pool99`), yet get `401 Unauthorized` from our API Gateway **HTTP API JWT Authorizer** when sending their Cognito Access Token! Walk through `iss`, `aud` vs `client_id`, `token_use` (`id` vs `access`), and custom scope/claim enforcement.
expectations: Activates the aws-auth skill

Checks exact issuer URL (`https://cognito-idp.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/ap-south-1_Pool99` with no trailing slash), `audience` (`app client id` — noting Cognito ID tokens put app client ID in `aud` while Cognito Access tokens put it in `client_id`, which HTTP API JWT Authorizer validates against `Audience`), and `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` header

Compares HTTP API JWT Authorizer (plus scope checks) vs REST API `COGNITO_USER_POOLS` Authorizer (where Cognito Access tokens require custom OAuth scopes configured on the method, otherwise REST authorizer expects an ID token!) and reminds validating custom tenant/role claims in backend logic (`aws-jwt-verify`)

evals.prompt: 50 users signed up yesterday and are stuck in `UNCONFIRMED` status because our SES sandbox blocked verification emails. Support wants to run a loop calling `admin-confirm-sign-up` on all 50 accounts right now! Explain the hidden security hazard of `admin-confirm-sign-up` and give the safe remediation.
expectations: Activates the aws-auth skill

Warns that **`admin-confirm-sign-up` flips user status to `CONFIRMED` WITHOUT verifying `email_verified=true`**, meaning users never proved ownership of the email address (breaking password reset delivery or enabling account-linking/pre-hijack risks!)

Recommends exiting SES sandbox first and having users verify ownership via **`resend-confirmation-code` -> `confirm-sign-up`** (reserving `admin-confirm-sign-up` strictly for pre-verified enterprise migrations)

evals.prompt: After signing into our Cognito User Pool, authenticated browser users need temporary AWS credentials to upload files ONLY into their own S3 prefix `s3://customer-vault/${cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:sub}/*`. Design the User Pool -> Identity Pool wiring and least-privilege IAM role.
expectations: Activates the aws-auth skill
Wires the Cognito User Pool + App Client as an authentication provider on a **Cognito Identity Pool** with **unauthenticated (guest) access disabled**

Scopes the Identity Pool authenticated IAM role trust policy (`cognito-identity.amazonaws.com`, `amr: authenticated`, `cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:aud`) and scopes S3 `PutObject`/`GetObject` strictly to `arn:aws:s3:::customer-vault/${cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:sub}/*`

evals.prompt: We want to inject `tenant_id` and `org_role` custom claims into **Cognito Access Tokens** (not just ID Tokens!) using a **Pre Token Generation Lambda Trigger** on a brand-new User Pool on the Lite / Essentials / Plus feature plans. What feature-plan gating and trigger version (`V1_0` vs `V2_0`/`V3_0`) rules must we check first?
expectations: Activates the aws-auth skill

Flags the critical warning: while `V1_0` Pre Token Generation customizes **ID tokens** on entry-level tiers, **customizing Access Tokens (`V2_0` / `V3_0` `claimsAndScopeOverrideDetails.accessTokenGeneration`) requires a paid Cognito feature plan** (such as Essentials / Plus — verify against current Cognito feature plans docs rather than assuming Lite supports it!)

evals.prompt: How do we modernize a Cognito User Pool to support **Passkey / WebAuthn** passwordless sign-in alongside TOTP MFA, AND enable **Cognito Threat Protection** (compromised-credential blocking + risk-based adaptive MFA)?
expectations: Activates the aws-auth skill
Configures choice-based `USER_AUTH` authentication flow (`ALLOW_USER_AUTH` on the app client + `AllowedFirstAuthFactors` including `WEB_AUTHN` with Relying Party ID matching domain, plus TOTP MFA)

Covers Cognito **Threat Protection** (Plus tier / Advanced Security: blocking compromised credentials, adaptive risk-based MFA challenges on anomalous IP/device logins, and exporting auth threat events to KMS-encrypted CloudWatch Logs)

evals.prompt: Inspect `ap-south-1` in our live AWS account (read-only) for any Amazon Cognito User Pools (`cognito-idp:ListUserPools`) and Identity Pools (`cognito-identity:ListIdentityPools`), and summarize the key security headers and token-handling controls we should enforce on any web app using Cognito.
expectations: Activates the aws-auth skill and queries `cognito-idp:ListUserPools` and `cognito-identity:ListIdentityPools` in `ap-south-1` via connected AWS MCP tools with zero raw `aws` CLI shell commands

Accurately reports live `ap-south-1` Cognito inventory (cleanly reporting 0 pools if none exist) and summarizes browser/API security hardening (PKCE, no SPA secret, `cookieStorage` + refresh token rotation/revocation, `Content-Security-Policy`, `HSTS`, `X-Frame-Options`/`frame-ancestors`, `aws-jwt-verify`)
Makes zero mutating AWS calls

evals.prompt: A corporate user's laptop was just stolen! Compare what **`GlobalSignOut` / `AdminUserGlobalSignOut`**, **`RevokeToken`**, and **`AdminDisableUser`** actually invalidate (and what stays valid until `exp`!) in Amazon Cognito.
expectations: Activates the aws-auth skill

Clarifies that `GlobalSignOut` / `AdminUserGlobalSignOut` and `RevokeToken` (`EnableTokenRevocation=true`) invalidate **Refresh Tokens** (and Cognito `GetUser`/API-validated sessions), **NOT stateless local-JWKS-verified ID/Access JWTs already issued**, which remain cryptographically valid until their `exp` timestamp unless short access-token TTLs (e.g., 5–15 min) or server-side revocation/denylist checks are used!
Explains pairing `AdminUserGlobalSignOut` + `AdminDisableUser` with short `AccessTokenValidity` (5–15 minutes)

evals.prompt: Query AWS documentation via connected AWS documentation tools to verify the exact **AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) region requirement** and parent-domain DNS record prerequisite when configuring a **Custom Domain** (`auth.example.com`) for Amazon Cognito Managed Login / Hosted UI on a User Pool in `ap-south-1`!
expectations: Queries connected AWS documentation MCP tools (`awsknowledge`, `aws-mcp`, or `awsiac`) with zero raw `aws` CLI commands

Confirms two classic Cognito Custom Domain gotchas even when the User Pool is in `ap-south-1`: (1) the **ACM TLS certificate MUST be in `us-east-1` (N. Virginia)** because Cognito Custom Domains deploy an AWS-managed CloudFront distribution under the hood, and (2) the **parent domain (`example.com`) MUST have a resolvable `A` record** at `create-user-pool-domain` time (plus adding the returned CloudFront `Alias`/`CNAME` target for `auth.example.com`)
